hooks.name: Translation Sync
hooks.description: When Rust source files in the GUI crate are edited, ensures POTFILES.in includes the file and rejects Rust-only \u{...} escapes in translatable strings

action.prompt:
A Rust source file in rustconn/src/ was edited. First, quickly check if the file contains any `i18n(` calls. If it does NOT contain `i18n(`, do nothing — stop here.

Only if the file DOES contain `i18n(` calls:
1. Verify the file is listed in `po/POTFILES.in`. If NOT listed, add it in alphabetical order within the GUI application source files section. Exception: do NOT add transient scratch/probe files that are about to be deleted — a POTFILES.in entry pointing at a missing file breaks po/update-pot.sh.
2. If a new file was added to POTFILES.in, inform the developer to run `po/update-pot.sh` to regenerate the .pot template.
3. Run `./scripts/check-i18n-escapes.sh`. It must print OK. If it FAILS, the file has a Rust-only `\u{...}` escape inside a translatable literal: xgettext runs with --language=C, cannot decode that escape, and copies it verbatim into the msgid — so the runtime lookup (where rustc has already decoded the literal) never matches and the string renders untranslated in every locale, even though the .po files report 100% complete. Report the offending file:line and fix it by putting the character directly in the literal (ASCII apostrophe is the project convention, cf. i18n("Don't Save") in rustconn/src/alert.rs). If the msgid already exists in po/*.po under the escaped form, rename it there too rather than leaving a stale entry.

Do NOT read the full file content — just check for the presence of `i18n(` pattern.
